content.title: About
content.content: Potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes that are deep‑fried until crisp and then seasoned with a variety of flavorings. The “other flavored” range includes creative blends such as barbecue, sour cream & onion, cheese & onion, chili‑lime and more.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial potato chip brand appeared in the United States in 1853.
There are more than 3,000 officially registered chip flavors worldwide.
In Russia, popular flavors include “Crab”, “Sour Cream & Onion”, and “Sweet‑Barbecue”.
Chips are often used in culinary experiments: crushed as a coating, added to salads, or even incorporated into desserts.
Most flavorings are derived from natural extracts, though artificial additives are sometimes used to boost taste.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Potato chips provide quick‑digesting carbohydrates that supply rapid energy.

items.title: Vitamin C content
items.content: When processed properly, a portion of vitamin C is retained, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chips contain potassium and iron, essential for normal bodily functions.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: If made from whole‑potato slices, they can contribute a modest amount of fiber.

items.title: Pleasurable taste
items.content: Moderate consumption can improve mood thanks to enjoyable flavor sensations.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds significant calories and saturated fats.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excess sodium may contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some flavorings may contain dairy, gluten, or soy ingredients.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Use of partially hydrogenated oils can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Certain chips contain artificial colors and preservatives that can trigger sensitivities in some individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chips are typically enjoyed as a snack on their own, with dips (sour cream, ketchup, cheese sauce) or as a crunchy topping for salads, burgers, and sandwiches. For a healthier option, choose baked chips with reduced salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from light. Once opened, transfer them to an airtight container to maintain crispness and prevent fat oxidation.
